title: Why Are States Fighting Over Student Loans for Nurses?
summary: Imagine you want to become a nurse practitioner or a nurse anesthetist—jobs that help save lives. You need extra school after college, but it's expensive. Now, a new rule from the government says you can't borrow as much money for that school. That's making a lot of people upset! Right now, 24 states and Washington, D.C., are suing the Trump administration over this rule. They say it will stop talented people from becoming nurses and other healthcare workers, especially in rural areas where there aren't enough doctors. Here's what changed: Before, graduate students could borrow up to the full cost of their program. Now, most can only borrow $20,500 a year, with a total limit of $100,000. Some degrees, like medicine and law, can borrow more—up to $50,000 a year and $200,000 total. But nursing, physical therapy, and nurse anesthesia didn't make the list of 'professional' degrees that get the higher limit. The American Nurses Association says this rule will hurt communities. They warn that students might have to take out expensive private loans or give up on advanced training. The government argues that most nursing degrees still fit under the new caps and that it will force colleges to lower prices. But the states suing say the rule is unfair and based on an old list from the 1950s, when many of these programs didn't even exist. This fight matters because if fewer people can afford to become advanced nurses, it could mean longer waits and less care for patients—maybe even you or your family someday.
why_it_matters: If fewer people can afford to train as advanced nurses, it could mean that when you or your family get sick, there won't be enough specialists to help you right away.

background_read: Under the Trump administration (President Donald Trump's government, in office since January 2025), the Department of Education changed loan limits for graduate school.

The list of 'professional' degrees that get higher borrowing limits was created in the 1950s, long before jobs like nurse anesthetist were common. The American Nurses Association (an organization representing millions of U.S. nurses) argues this hurts rural areas that already have too few healthcare workers.
Rural areas often struggle to attract enough doctors and nurses, so limiting training funds could make healthcare harder to find for families living there.
Article_Structure: WHO: 24 states, Washington D.C., the Trump administration, and the American Nurses Association
WHAT: A new federal rule caps graduate student loans and excludes nursing from higher borrowing limits, sparking a lawsuit
WHERE: Across the United States, especially affecting rural areas with few healthcare workers
WHY: The rule relies on a 1950s professional-degree list, risking a shortage of advanced nurses and longer patient wait times

perspectives.description: They believe setting lower loan caps will pressure graduate schools to lower their prices, making education more affordable in the long run.
They argue the rule is unfair because it uses a decades-old list and will stop many qualified people from entering healthcare, harming patients.
They feel stuck because they might not be able to afford the extra training needed to become nurse practitioners, even though they want to help people.
